prompt:
We're retiring docs/billing.md. Please move what belongs beside the code into comments in the code.

Input files: AGENTS.md, README.md, billing/__init__.py, billing/lines.py, billing/totals.py, docs/billing.md, docs/setup.md, tests/__init__.py, tests/test_billing.py
assertions: The FIN-88 rounding reason is in a code comment or docstring, and no document states it apart from AGENTS.md, which must not be edited.
The packing-slip reason for keeping lines in SKU order is in a code comment or docstring and in no document.
The rounding reason sits at invoice_total (or CENT) in billing/totals.py, and the packing-slip reason at invoice_lines (placement, heuristic).
The "Who to ask" notes (the FINQ queue and the accounts-receivable lead) are each in exactly one document and in no code comment or docstring.
No added comment or docstring repeats the page's restatement of the code (invoice_total adds the line amounts and returns a Decimal; invoice_lines returns the order's lines).
No code changed: every Python file's code is the same apart from comments and docstrings.
Every original comment and docstring is kept word for word, AGENTS.md is byte-for-byte unchanged although it repeats the FIN-88 rule, and README.md and docs/setup.md lose nothing.
No file was added to the repository.
The reply says where the moved facts went, naming billing/totals.py (or invoice_total) and billing/lines.py (or invoice_lines).
The reply tells the user, in one bullet or paragraph, that AGENTS.md also states the FIN-88 rounding rule.
The reply gives a fate for each claim on the page: the invoice_total restatement, the FIN-88 reason, the packing-slip reason and the Who to ask notes.
